name: Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship (Erasmus School of Economics)
requiredDocuments: Motivation letter (max. two A4, Arial 11): stating motivation to study at Erasmus School of Economics, evidence of being an excellent student, and why the scholarship would expand the opportunity to study there
Financial statement (max. one A4, Arial 11): describing your financial situation and the reason/need to receive the scholarship
Budget plan: overview of how you plan to finance your studies if awarded, using the EUR Budget plan template
Certified copy of your most recent academic transcript (must carry a wet stamp and signature of a school official; screenshots of online portals are NOT accepted)
Certified statement from your educational institution confirming your obtained GPA (EUR GPA template may be used)

timeline.deadline: 31 January 2026, 23:59 (application portal listed as open 1 December 2025 – 1 February 2026)
timeline.notes: Dates are for the 2026-2027 cycle as published on the official ESE page. As of 2026-06-18 this cycle is CLOSED (the page is headed 'Application closed'); the 2027-2028 cycle had not opened at verification time. The 2027-2028 window is expected to follow the same ~Dec–Jan pattern but was not yet published. Separately, the EUR-wide Trustfonds/TSH Changemaker page noted info for 2027–2028 'will be available in the autumn'.

benefits: Full tuition fee waiver — for non-EEA/EU students the full €21,000 institutional fee is covered (€2,695 waived via the scholarship + €18,305 paid by the school); for EEA/EU students the €2,695 statutory fee is waived
Living allowance of €1,200 per month = €14,400 for one academic year (paid to the student)
One-time personal allowance of €249 (paid to the student)
mustKnow: ONE YEAR ONLY: the scholarship applies to a single academic year and can be received only once — a 2-year master's is NOT fully covered for the second year

ELIGIBILITY VARIES BY FACULTY: the ESE (economics) track is explicitly open to non-EEA applicants, but other EUR faculty versions differ — e.g. the ESHPM 'Erasmus Trust Fund' track is restricted to EEA/EU nationals only. A Bangladeshi must apply through a track that admits non-EEA students (ESE does).
Demonstrated FINANCIAL NEED is mandatory: a detailed financial statement and budget plan describing how you would finance your studies are required, not just merit
Minimum bachelor average of 7.50 on a 1–10 scale ('excellent' study results) is required
Must NEVER have been enrolled before as a full-degree master student at a Dutch institution (a prior ESE pre-master is allowed)

Must be admitted to one of three ESE master's: Accounting, Auditing & Control; Econometrics & Management Science; or Economics & Business. An admission offer is not required at application but only admitted students are considered.
Two-step: you must first register/apply to the master programme in Studielink + EUR Application Portal, then submit the scholarship application via Osiris before the deadline

Immigration procedure must be completed (submit immigration docs + transfer tuition + living-cost deposit + IND fee); scholarship applicants are told to send the immigration application by May, hard deadline 10 July
Only one type of EUR scholarship is awarded per applicant — you may apply for several but cannot combine awards

universities: Erasmus University Rotterdam — Erasmus School of Economics

duration: Scholarship covers 1 academic year (programmes are typically 1-year MSc; some 2-year)
eligibleNationalities: Open to both EEA and non-EEA nationals on the Erasmus School of Economics track (no closed country list); non-EEA nationals such as Bangladeshis are explicitly addressed in the funding terms. Note: some other EUR faculty tracks of the Trustfonds scholarship are EEA/EU-only.
minGPA: Bachelor average of at least 7.50 on a 1–10 scale
